## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
READ 06-CLOSE-REPORT.md SECOND, straight after this file: its first word says
whether the baton is finished, and that is the only thing you need before
deciding what to pick up. Then 04-NEXT-LOOPS-PRIORITIZED.md, then 01.

WHAT THIS SESSION WAS, in one sentence: BrotherMode's hooks no longer need a
POSIX shell, its gate verdict now reaches a Bitbucket remote as well as a
GitHub one, and an external Bitbucket remediation plan was checked claim by
claim rather than accepted.

THE ONE THING TO KNOW BEFORE TOUCHING THE HOOKS. The Stop and PreCompact
chains no longer spell their programs out in the hook command string. They
name tools/bm_hookchain.py and a chain name, and the programs live in that
file's CHAINS table, which is now their single copy. Four controls used to
read those programs out of the command string, and every one of them was
taught to read the table instead: the consent inventory, the benchmark
parser, the process-count pins, and the Stop contract in the view suite.
The last of those was found by the FULL BATTERY rather than by the per-suite
runs, because it lives in a suite nobody would search for hook wiring. If
you add a fifth reader, read the table.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, and must not be described as if it were: no Windows
machine has run any of this. The wiring can run without a shell, which is
what tools/test_bm_hooks.py checks; whether it BEHAVES correctly on Windows
is unverified, and docs/WINDOWS-CHECK.md is the protocol that closes it.
